2. Respondent Nos.1 and 2 as plaintiffs filed the said title suit in the Court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka for declaration of title to the suit land on the averments, inter-alia, that the land of C.S. khatian No. 241 being plot No. 390/3940 measuring an area of 0568 ajutangsha originally belonged to Khiroda Shundari Daishya which was put to auction for arrear of rent in certificate Case No. 660 of 1952-53 and was purchased by Ali Ahmed @ Dr. Monjurul Hoque, son of late Munshi Nowab Ali of 74, Mirpur, Dhaka on 20.06.1953. The sale was confirmed on 24.08.1953 and sale certificate was issued in favour of said Ali Ahmed on 19.11.1953. The auction purchaser (Ali Ahmed) got possession of the auction purchased land on 20.01.1954 through court. Ali Ahmed being in possession of the auction purchased land (hereinafter referred to as the suit property) for more than 12 years mutated his name in the Government record and paid rents accordingly; S.A. Khatian being No.197 and R.S. Khatian being No.1248 were prepared in his name. Ali Ahmed while had been in possession of the suit property died issueless on 18.06.1975 leaving behind a widow, named, Khatibunnassa who inherited the entire suit property as her 4 annas share as his wife and the remaining 12 annas share because of the 'Doctrine of Return'. Khatibunnesa being the 16 annas owner of the suit property died on 10.02.78 leaving behind her only full brother Abdul Mannan who inherited the entire property of his deceased sister. While Abdul Mannan had been in possession of the suit property as the 16 annas owner, by a registered heba-bil-ewaj dated 29.11.79 being No. 45060 transferred the suit property in favour of the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs being minors their father Abdul Majid as their natural guardian took over the possession of the transferred land. Thus the plaintiffs being the 16 annas owners of the suit property have been in peaceful possession thereof. Defendants having no right, title, interest and possession in the suit property by resorting to various tactics created forged papers and tried to take possession of the suit property forcibly, but due to the intervention of the respectable people of the mahalla failed. On 06.07.80 the defendants along with the process server of the Court and the police attacked (in the plaint in Bengali it has been written as “��ামলা চালায়” in the peaceful possession of the plaintiffs by showing a decree. The bailiff of the Court having seen the valid title documents of the plaintiffs failed to execute the decree in Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1980. However, after making inquiry from the bailiff of the Court the father of the plaintiffs Abdul Mazid came to know that the defendants obtained a fraudulent decree on 15.11.79 in Title Suit No. 62 of 1979 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka. On further query the plaintiffs came to know that a so-called bainapatra to sell the suit property allegedly entered into by one Rasheda Begum, wife of Salimuddin of 321, Lalbag Road, Dhaka on 12.08.92 with the defendants was the basis of the said decree. Rasheda Begum went to Pakistan Via Nepal after liberation of Bangladesh, so the alleged bainapatra was fraudulent and was not legally enforceable in respect of the suit property. Rasheda Begum had no right, title, interest and possession in the suit property. Therefore, the defendants did not acquire any title to the suit property either on the basis of the bainapatra or their alleged purchase. The plaintiffs themselves and through their predecessor have been in possession of the suit property for more than 12 years since the purchase of the same in auction. The defendants got a kabala executed and registered in their names through court in execution of the ex-parte decree passed in the said suit, but by the said kabala they did not acquire right, tide and interest in the suit property. As neither the plaintiffs nor their predecessor were made parties in Title Suit No. 62 of 1979, the decree passed therein suit was not binding upon them. The defendants were not entitled to get any relief by way of execution of the decree through Title Execution No. 3 of 1980 without filing a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khash possession on payment of a advalorem court fees. The plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 329 of 1980 in Court of Munsif, 3rd Court, Dhaka against the defendants for permanent injunction which was decreed on 28.03.84 on contest. Against the said decree the defendants filed Title Appeal No. 196 of 1984 before the District Judge, Dhaka. The learned Subordinate Judge and Commercial Court No. 2, Dhaka who heard the appeal allowed the same by judgment and decree dated 24.01.1987 and dismissed the suit. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed in the said appeal the plaintiffs filed Civil Revision No. 76 of 1987 before this Division, but the rule was discharged on 27.05.92 and thus decree passed by the appellate court was up-held. Against the judgment and order passed in the said civil revision the plaintiffs filed Petition For Leave To Appeal No. 297 of 1972 before the Appellate Division. The leave petition was dismissed by the Appellate Division observing as under: 

 3. When the defendants tried to take possession of the suit property through Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1980 without filing any suit for title and recovery of khash possession the plaintiffs on 27.10.93 filed an application under Order 21, rule 99 of the Code of Civil Procedure for dismissing the execution case. The learned Subordinate Judge by his order dated 29.01.94 rejected the said application. Though the defendants failed to dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit property through the said execution case, they were telling the people of the Mahalla that in an opportune moment they would take possession of the suit property by dispossessing the plaintiffs therefrom. The defendants are very powerful and rich persons having so many `goondas' at their disposal and they might dispossess the plaintiffs at any time causing irreparable loss and damage to them. The cause of action for the suit arose on 21.10.93 when the defendants along with the bailiff asked the plaintiffs to hand over vacant possession of the suit property to them and the same was continuing. 

 5. The plaintiffs amended the plaint further praying for declaration of title, recovery of khash possession and for mesne profit from 16.09.97 to till the delivery of possession of the suit property to them along with interest at the rate of 16 % stating, inter-alia, that during the pendency of the suit the plaintiffs became major on 07.10.95 and 15.10.96 respectively. While the suit was at the stage of peremptory hearing the defendants having understood that they would be defeated in the suit they along with 20/25 terrorists being armed with dangerous weapons entered into the suit property forcibly on 16.09.97 and evicted the plaintiffs and their men therefrom and looted away the household articles worth taka 6,00,000/00. In the similar way the defendants also looted away the goods from 10 (ten) family rooms and 13 (thirteen) shops in the suit property and took possession thereof. The plaintiffs used to get rent from the tenants of the said family rooms and shops to the tune of taka 26,000/00 per month. After the incident Mr. Abdul Majid, the father of the plaintiffs lodged a complaint with Lalbagh Police Station informing the police the said fact of illegal eviction and looting of goods by the defendants and their terrorist which being treated as First Information Report was registered as Lalbag Police Station Case No. 32(9)97 under sections 144/447/44 and 380 of the Penal Code. On behalf of the tenants one Wazir Ahmed also lodged a complaint with the said police station which was registered as Lalbag P.S. Case No. 940 dated 16.09.97. Subsequently by applying illegal force on the father of the plaintiffs the defendants got some paper signed by him to the effect that he would not proceed with the criminal case as well as civil suit. The defendants by putting threat on the life of the plaintiffs as well as their father Abdul Majid and also by applying force got a white paper signed by them with the writing to the effect “১৬,৬০,০০০/- টাকা বুঝিয়া পাইলাম” though they received no money from the defendants. The defendants demolished the entire one storied building and the shop rooms standing on the suit land causing a loss of taka 20 lacs to the plaintiffs. Because of the eviction of the plaintiffs from their one storied building, from the semi pucca family quarters and the 13 (thirteen) shops on 16.09.97 the plaintiffs are being deprived of their monthly income to the tune of taka 26,000/-, so they were entitled to get mesne profit at the said rate from the said date. 

 11. Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali, the learned Advocate appearing for the appellants submitted that the plaintiffs claimed their title to the suit property on the basis of alleged auction sale which took place on 20.06.53, whereas the defendants vendor's vendor purchased the suit property from the admitted owners on 27.03.1953, therefore, the plaintiffs predecessor did not acquire any title to the suit property by virtue of the alleged auction purchase. Mr. Mohammad Ali further submitted that previously the plaintiffs vendor's predecessor Dr. Manjurul Haque @ Ali Ahmed made an attempt to nullify the result of Money Suit No. 50 of 1959 and House Rent Case No. 598 of 1959 filed by the defendant's vendor Rasheda Begum against him and his wife by obtaining signatures on two applications showing withdrawal of the suit and the case which were ultimately set aside in Title Suit No. 221 of 1984 of the Court of Munsif, 3rd Court, Dhaka and thus the title of defendant's vendor was recognised in the said suit, the plaintiffs could not have any title through said Manjurul Haque, so their suit was liable to be dismissed. Mr. Mohammad Ali further submitted that previously plaintiffs filed Title Suit No. 329 of 1980 in the Court of Munsif, 3rd Court, Dhaka against the present defendants which they lost up to the Appellate Division and moreso, in the alleged two agreements created by Ali Ahmed in the name of Rasheda Begum on 16.11.59 which were cancelled in Title Suit No. 221 of 1964, the plaintiffs predecessor Ali Ahmed having claimed 7 annas share only in the suit property by virtue of his alleged auction purchase the plaintiffs could not claim the entire suit property and in fact their suit was clearly barred by the principle of constructive resjudicata, and, as such, their suit was liable to be dismissed. Mr. Mohammad Ali further submitted that the sale certificate allegedly issued in favour of Ali Ahmed does not tally with form 28 and rule 74 printed and framed respectively under the rules framed under the Public Demands Recovery Act, so the auction was doubtful and by such auction purchase no title accrued to said Ali Ahmed and consequently the plain-tiffs did not acquire any title to the suit property, therefore, they were not entitled to get any relief as prayed for. Mr. Mohammad Ali further submitted that the plaintiffs having voluntarily vacated the suit property by delivering the possession thereof to the defendants on receipt of a sum of taka 16,60,600/00 the instant suit for recovery of khash possession was not maintainable in law, the learned sub-ordinate judge erred in law in decreeing the suit and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside and the appeal be allowed. 

 25. Admittedly the plaintiffs had been in possession of the suit property which was clearly found by all the courts in connection with the proceedings which arose out of Title Suit No. 329 of 1980 of the Court of Munsif, 3rd Court, Dhaka. The plaintiffs by amending the plaint prayed for recovery of khas possession of the suit property and also for mesne profit stating categorically that the defendants dispossessed them and their tenants therefrom forcibly on 16.09.1997. All along plaintiff's case was that their predecessor's predecessor Ali Ahmed got possession of the suit property through court on the basis of his auction purchase and in support of their said case they filed the writ of delivery of possession, exhibit 2 (ka). From exhibit 1 (ka) and 1 (kha) it appears that the S.A. and R.S. khatians were prepared in the name of Ali Ahmed. Exhibit 5 shows that plaintiffs names were mutated and a new khatian being No. 197 was opened in their names. Exhibit 6-6 (Na) series show that Ali Ahmed paid rents to the government and then the plaintiffs paid rents to the government after mutation of their names. Exhibit 7-7 (Nia) series show that the holding in respect of the suit property was recorded with the Dhaka City Corporation in the name of the plaintiffs and they paid City Corporation tax. Exhibits 8. 9 and 10 series show that it is the plaintiffs who paid the utility bills such as Dhaka Was a, gas and electricity in respect of the suit property. Exhibits 11 and 12 series show that the plaintiffs inducted tenants in the suit property who paid rents to them. And those documents primafacie proved that it was Ali Ahmed and the plaintiffs who exercised their right of ownership in the suit property and had been in possession thereof uninterruptedly since the delivery of possession on 20.01.54 by virtue of the auction purchase. On the other hand, the contesting defendants failed to file a single scrape of paper to show that their so-called vendor Rasheda Begum and before that Salimunnesa ever exercised their right of ownership and possession in the suit property or that Ali Ahmed or his wife had ever attorned Salimunnessa as land lord after purchase from Khiroda Sundari Daishya and Lalit Mohan Shaha or they ever paid any rent to Rasheda Begum attorning as their land lord. Not only that the defendants also failed to file/produce any original deed of their alleged vendor Rasheda Begum. It is a well settled legal proposition that though the khatians and rent receipts are not the documents of title, yet they can very much be used for collateral purpose to prove title. The very fact that S.A. and R.S. khatians were prepared in the name of Ali Ahmed and he paid rents to the government and after his death the plaintiffs paid rents and they also paid other utility bills proved their title to the suit property. It is also a salutory legal proposition that possession follows title, so even if it is presumed for argument's sake that the plaintiff's vendor's vendor Ali Ahmed purchased the 7th share of the suit plot as argued by Mr. A.J. Mohammad Ali, yet due to the long and continuous uninterrupted possession in the suit property since 20.01.1954, the plaintiffs acquired absolute title to the suit property. 

 30. So, the plaintiffs could not be evicted from the suit property other that due process of law. The defendants levied Title Execution Case No. 3 of 1980 in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 3rd Court, Dhaka for execution of the decree. The defendants admitted in the written statement that though the bailiff went to the suit property yet he could not deliver possession thereof to them because of the resistance put by the plaintiffs. The plaintiffs specific case was that the defendants dispossessed them and their tenants forcibly on 16.09.97 and looted away the goods for which they amended the plaint and prayed for recovery of khas possession along with other reliefs including mesne profit. Whereas the defendant's case was that the plaintiffs of their own delivered vacant possession of the suit property to them on 05.10.97 on receipt of, a sum of taka 16,60,000/00 on 30.09.97 on the basis of a salish/mediation done by Hajee Md. Selim, the local member of the parliament and the other respectable people of the locality. Defendant's further case was that Abdul Majid, father of the plaintiffs acknowledged the receipt of the said amount of money in writing in a paper by putting his signature which was subsequently signed by plaintiff No. 2 on 05.10.97. P.W.1 categorically denied the said assertion of the defendants. In support of the forcible dispossession by the defendants from the suit property the plaintiffs besides examining plaintiff No. 2 as p.w.1 also examined 3 (three) other witnesses and filed documentary evidence. P.W.1 in his examination-in-chief categorically stated that while the suit was pending the defendants entered into the suit property along with 20/30 terrorists and dispossessed them and looted away the goods which included gold ornaments. The defendants also looted away the goods of their tenants. P.W.1 further stated that over the said incident their father lodged a complaint with Lalbag Police Station which gave rise to Case No. 32 (9) 97. On behalf of the 'bharatias' Wazir Ahmed also lodged a general dairy with Lalbag Police Station being No. 940 dated 16.09.97. The certified copy of the First Information Report (FIR) was filed and marked as exhibit 16 and the copy of the general diary was filed and marked as exhibit 17. The p. w. further stated that the news of their illegal eviction from the suit property and the looting away of goods therefrom were published in the daily Inquilab and the Bhorer Kagaj on 18.09.97 and 20.09.97 respectively. The copies of the said news papers were filed and marked as exhibits 18 series. P.W.1 further deposed that on 30.09.97 the defendants by force obtained a writing from his father in a white paper to the effect that he received taka 16,60,000/00 and then on 05.10.75 also obtained a similar writing from him in the same paper though they did not receive any money. In cross-examination p.w.1 further asserted that no salish took place on 30.09.97 at the house of the ex-member of the parliament. Hajee Selim at the presence of the plaintiffs and the Ward Commissioner and they did not put their signature on receipt of a sum of taka 16,60,000/00 (sixteen lacs sixty thousand). P.W.1 further asserted that his signature was obtained in the receipt on 05.10.97 by force. P.W.2, Abdul Majid, the father of the plaintiffs categorically stated in his examination-in-chief that Rasheda Begum was never the owner of the suit property and she never possessed the same and Title Suit No. 106 of 1970 filed by her for declaration of title was dismissed for default. This P.W. further stated that on 16.09.97 the defendants being accompanied by 20/25 goondas dispossessed the plaintiffs and their bharatias by force and looted away the goods. After eviction the defendants took him to court forcibly and got the suit withdrawn on the threat that if he did not withdraw the suit they would kill his sons (the plaintiffs). On 30.09.97 the defendants took him to their office and then got a paper written by him to the effect that he received taka sixteen lacs and sixty thousand. At first it was written as 16,000/00. He further stated that he did not receive any money from the defendants. P.W.2 denied the defendant's case that he, on 30.09.97 in presence of the former member of the parliament Hajee Selim and others demanded taka 20,00,000/00 (twenty lacs) from the defendants as compensation and on receipt of taka 16,60,000/00 delivered possession of the suit property and withdrew the civil and criminal cases. This p. w. corroborated P.W.1 on all other points. By cross-examining these two P.W. s the defendants could not at all shake the credibility of their testimony in examination-in-chief.
